sections.body:
## Why rope access for inspection

Inspection often needs only a short time at each point, but the points are spread out at height. Scaffolding for that costs time and money out of proportion to the job. A rope access team reaches point after point in a working day and hands over data the same or next day.

## Who does the testing

Visual inspection is carried out by rope access technicians trained to read structural condition. For NDT methods such as ultrasonic thickness (UT), magnetic particle (MPI), or penetrant testing (PT), testing is done by personnel qualified in that method, with the rope access technicians providing access and safety.

## Data you can use

Every finding is logged with location, photos, and measurements, so the report supports maintenance decisions, audits, and comparison with the next inspection.

columns.title: Scope of work
items: Close visual inspection of steel and concrete structures
Ultrasonic thickness (UT) on tanks, pipes, and chimneys
Weld inspection by MPI or PT by qualified personnel
Photo and video records per point

columns.title: What you receive
items: An inspection report with photos per finding
Measurement data in an auditable format
An indexed photo and video archive

sections.title: Four steps from survey to report

items.title: 1. Survey & quotation
items.text: We review the site or your photos and drawings, then send the scope, method, schedule, and a written quotation.

items.title: 2. Work plan & permits
items.text: A risk assessment, method statement, and rescue plan are prepared before work starts; permits are arranged with the site manager.

items.title: 3. Delivery
items.text: A team of Kemnaker-certified technicians works with a supervisor on site; the area below the work zone is secured.

items.title: 4. Report & handover
items.text: Before-and-after photos and a work report are handed over with recommendations for the next maintenance cycle.

items.q: Can the inspection results be used for audits?
items.a: Yes. The report lists location, method, photos, and measurements for every point, so it is traceable and comparable with the next inspection.

items.q: How long does an inspection take?
items.a: It depends on the number of points and the height. Rigging a rope access system usually takes only a few hours, so most of the time goes into the inspection itself.
Visual inspection and most NDT can be done while the asset is operating, provided the permit to work and safety conditions are met.

sections.title: Tell us about the job
sections.text: Send the location, the type of building or asset, and your target dates. We reply with a written quotation, usually the same working day.
